top_story: Iran is tightening internal control as it moves to criminalize contact with foreign media and hands a photojournalist a 15-year sentence, widening the space in which ordinary civic activity can be recast as a security offense. Two days later, Washington targeted Banque Misr’s UAE branches for allegedly moving more than $1 billion through Iranian shadow banking networks, underscoring how pressure on Iran now extends through Gulf-based financial channels and draws Arab institutions into the sanctions arena. In Gaza, the slower but equally consequential collapse of hospital equipment under spare-parts restrictions is stripping basic care from civilians, with oxygen access and routine treatment becoming contingent on a blockade regime rather than medical need. The combined picture is a region where coercive state tools—financial, legal, and logistical—are intensifying across borders and falling most heavily on civic space and civilian survival.
